## B — Audience and scope
The audience is an New Hampshire first-time passenger-car applicant studying driver license and non-driver identification. sections.heading: C — Driver license and non-driver identification
sections.markdown:
## C — Licensing and examination knowledge
FACT_ID: sec02-F001 | anchor: P10
A Youth Operator license is issued from age 16 until the person reaches 21, according to the manual's license-type list.

FACT_ID: sec02-F002 | anchor: P10
Youth Operator licenses use a vertical layout and expire when the holder reaches the twenty-first birthday.

FACT_ID: sec02-F003 | anchor: P10
Restriction B identifies a corrective-lens requirement, while restriction C identifies a mechanical aid.

FACT_ID: sec02-F004 | anchor: P10
Restriction D refers to a prosthetic aid, and restriction E refers to an automatic transmission.

FACT_ID: sec02-F005 | anchor: P10
Restriction F specifies an outside mirror, while restriction G limits driving to daylight.

FACT_ID: sec02-F006 | anchor: P10
The license-restriction list uses IID for an ignition-interlock requirement and RTW for a three-wheel-motorcycle restriction.

FACT_ID: sec02-F007 | anchor: P10
A Youth Operator license holder who is younger than 18 may not drive during the period from one in the morning to four in the morning.

FACT_ID: sec02-F008 | anchor: P10
For the first six months of licensing, a driver under 18 may carry no more than one nonfamily passenger younger than 25 unless a licensed responsible adult aged at least 25 accompanies the driver.

FACT_ID: sec02-F009 | anchor: P10
A Youth Operator license holder younger than 18 cannot carry passengers beyond the number of available belts or safety restraints.

FACT_ID: sec02-F010 | anchor: P10
A driver under 18 may not use a mobile electronic device, including hands-free equipment, while driving or momentarily stopped in traffic except for an emergency report to the emergency system or a public-safety agency.

FACT_ID: sec02-F011 | anchor: P11
Residents may use another accepted identification document, such as a passport, instead of obtaining a REAL ID-compliant New Hampshire identification card for federal purposes.

FACT_ID: sec02-F012 | anchor: P11
A REAL ID-compliant license or identification card requires additional identifying documents; the manual directs applicants to DMV's document list.

FACT_ID: sec02-F013 | anchor: P11
New Hampshire residents aged at least 12 who lack a valid driver license may apply for a nondriver identification card.

FACT_ID: sec02-F014 | anchor: P11
A nondriver identification-card application requires the same identifying documentation used for a driver-license application.

FACT_ID: sec02-F015 | anchor: P11
A nondriver identification card can be issued in a REAL ID-compliant form.

FACT_ID: sec02-F016 | anchor: P11
A new resident holding a valid outside-state license normally needs only vision testing to obtain the New Hampshire license.

FACT_ID: sec02-F017 | anchor: P11
When an outside-state license has been expired for more than a year, the applicant must pass vision, knowledge and road testing.

FACT_ID: sec02-F018 | anchor: P11
An incoming resident applying for a different vehicle class must complete the written and road tests appropriate to that new class.

FACT_ID: sec02-F019 | anchor: P11
The handbook states that a New Hampshire license expires on its holder's birthday at five-year intervals.

FACT_ID: sec02-F020 | anchor: P11
The renewal reminder is sent to DMV's last recorded mailing address roughly two months before license expiration.

FACT_ID: sec02-F021 | anchor: P11
Renewal instructions explain an in-person application and, for an eligible applicant, an online application.

FACT_ID: sec02-F022 | anchor: P11
An applicant who expects to be temporarily outside the state at renewal may renew as much as six months early.

FACT_ID: sec02-F023 | anchor: P11
A driver leaving before renewal and returning after expiration must notify DMV in writing to qualify for the described six-month temporary license.

FACT_ID: sec02-F024 | anchor: P11
A driver who has not reported a mailing-address change, or whose privilege is suspended or revoked, will not receive the usual renewal notice.

FACT_ID: sec02-F025 | anchor: P11
The license holder remains responsible for renewing before expiration even when no reminder arrives.

Misconceptions: Treat closely related requirements as separate rules; preserve the triggering condition and any exception given in each fact [P10].
Mnemonics: Remember the condition together with the required action; this is an authored study cue.

sections.heading: C2 — Driver license and non-driver identification
sections.markdown:
## C2 — Licensing and examination knowledge
FACT_ID: sec02-F026 | anchor: P11
The manual describes no-cost renewal for an armed-forces member who held a valid New Hampshire license and state residence when beginning qualifying military service lasting at least two years.

FACT_ID: sec02-F027 | anchor: P12
After a hearing concerning specified offenses, a license holder under 20 can face an initial suspension or revocation lasting between 20 and 40 days.

FACT_ID: sec02-F028 | anchor: P12
The listed under-20 suspension or revocation range increases to 45 through 90 days for a second offense and 90 through 180 days for a third or later offense.

FACT_ID: sec02-F029 | anchor: P12
After a third or later qualifying offense, reinstatement also requires an approved driver-attitude course attended in person.

FACT_ID: sec02-F030 | anchor: P12
Youth Operators convicted of impaired driving, reckless operation or speeding more than 30 miles per hour above the limit face additional penalties.

FACT_ID: sec02-F031 | anchor: P12
Evidence of hazardous misuse of driving privileges, repeated disregard for safety, or a crash causing death or serious injury can support action against a young operator's license.

FACT_ID: sec02-F032 | anchor: P12
The manual identifies legal intoxication at an alcohol concentration of zero point zero eight percent, with a zero point zero two percent standard for drivers under 21.

FACT_ID: sec02-F033 | anchor: P12
Driving in New Hampshire implies consent to blood, breath, urine or combined testing following arrest for an alcohol or drug offense; refusing testing can cause loss of driving privileges.

FACT_ID: sec02-F034 | anchor: P12
Excessive demerit points may result in losing driving privileges, and the consequence can depend on the driver's age.

FACT_ID: sec02-F035 | anchor: P12
Violations such as speeding, ignoring signals or stop signs, impaired driving and improper passing can add demerit points.

FACT_ID: sec02-F036 | anchor: P12
An offense committed in another state may be reported to New Hampshire and affect the person's record or driving privileges.

FACT_ID: sec02-F037 | anchor: P12
A habitual-offender finding follows the required hearing and can result in revocation for one through four years under the handbook's account.

FACT_ID: sec02-F038 | anchor: P12
The manual states that driving after a habitual-offender declaration may lead to imprisonment lasting at least one year and as long as five years.
